description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Round 5. Verify the round-4 fixes (commit HEAD): the docs/qa recordings exemption (results[].video/.screenshot only), http-level security headers incl. the 421 refusal, the Host-guard static test, tools/container-smoke.mjs and its evidence file, the lint rule name-key and Intl/toLocale exemption, the theme e2e select handling and the widened static theme guard. Check against the spec delta and design.md. Do NOT re-report what design.md lists under "Accepted limits (review round 3)" or the documented backend-port and real-compose-stack follow-ups; report only defects in shipped behaviour or tests that can pass while the spec is violated.

findings.title: Intl/toLocale exemption also exempts literal UI text passed to Intl formatters (e.g. Intl.ListFormat)
findings.evidence:
`if (isLocaleFormatting(node.callee)) return literalTexts(node.callee.object);` drops every argument of any `.method()` called on `new Intl.X(...)`. Locale and options arguments sit on the constructor, not on `.format()`, so this branch only drops the value being formatted. For `

{new Intl.ListFormat('cs').format(['Matematika', 'Čeština'])}

` the receiver is a NewExpression, `literalTexts` falls to `default: []`, and the hard-coded Czech words are never reported (NFR-9). The opposite case also fails: `Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ').format(d)` without `new` is not recognised, so the locale string 'cs-CZ' is reported as UI text.
findings.suggestion: Exempt the arguments of `toLocale*`/`localeCompare` calls and of the `Intl.*` constructor or call. Keep scanning the arguments of `.format`/`.formatToParts` on an Intl instance, at least for ListFormat. Accept `Intl.X(...)` without `new` as well. Add an invalid test case for `new Intl.ListFormat('cs').format(['Ahoj'])`.

findings.title: Theme e2e skips a select's remaining options once one option navigates away
findings.evidence: Inside `for (const choice of choices)`, a pathname change triggers `await page.goto(screen.path); break;`. When the first option of a select navigates (for example a picker that changes route or reloads with a query), every later option is never selected. A later option that forces `data-theme` would then pass the test. The spec scenario requires every select on a route to be activated (spec.md line 25).
findings.suggestion: After navigating back, re-locate the select (`controls.nth(i)`) and `continue` with the next option instead of `break`. Alternatively, collect the choices first and run each one from a fresh `page.goto(screen.path)`.

findings.title: Static theme guard and e2e only see token redefinition on :root/html and the body background
findings.evidence: The token pattern `'(:root|html)\\s*\\{[^}]*--[\\w-]+\\s*:'` misses a theme forced by redefining `--paper` (or other tokens) on another selector, such as `.app-shell { --paper: … }` or `[data-route] { --ink: … }`. It also misses an inline style object `style={{ '--paper': x }}` and a class set from a variable, such as `classList.add(mode)` or `className={mode}`. The e2e only asserts `body` background-color and `[data-theme]` count, so a control that switches the shell container's tokens passes both checks.
findings.suggestion: Widen the CSS token check to any selector that redefines a design-system colour token (`--paper`, `--ink`, `--hero`, …) in app CSS. Flag `'--` keys in inline style objects. In the e2e, also assert the computed `--paper` (or background) of the route's `data-route` container, not just `body`.

findings.title: container-smoke evidence file leaves out the exception that caused a FAIL
findings.evidence: The catch block runs `failures.push(String(err.message ?? err))` but never adds to `results`. A docker build error or a `waitReady` timeout therefore writes `Result: FAIL (1)` with a table that has no failing row and does not name the error, and the Scope line says 'Playwright through nginx NOT included' with no reason. Separately, `writeFileSync('docs/qa/container-smoke-latest.md', …)` resolves against the cwd. Run from any other directory, it throws after cleanup with no summary line, so no evidence is written.
findings.suggestion: In the catch block, call `check('setup', false, err.message)` or push an equivalent row into `results`. Resolve the evidence path from `import.meta.url` (the repo root) rather than the cwd.

findings.title: Intl/toLocale exemption skips all format() arguments, so literal UI text passed to Intl.ListFormat is never linted (NFR-9)
findings.evidence:
For `new Intl.X(...).format(args)`, `isLocaleFormatting` matches the callee and returns `literalTexts(node.callee.object)`. That object is a NewExpression, which falls through to `default: return []` (line 107), so `.format()`'s arguments are never inspected. A feature dev can write `

{new Intl.ListFormat('cs').format(['Matematika', 'Čeština'])}

` and the screen shows hard-coded Czech ("Matematika a Čeština"), yet `doucko/no-literal-ui-text` stays green. This is a literal in the same file, which design.md says the rule catches ("literals nested in arrays"), so it is a regression from round 4, not the accepted cross-module limit. The pseudo-catalog render only catches it if a registered route renders that state.
findings.suggestion:
Exempt only the locale and options arguments: the constructor's arguments for `new Intl.*(locales, options)`, and the arguments of `toLocale*`/`localeCompare`. Keep linting the arguments of `.format()`/`.formatToParts()` on an Intl instance, or at least those of `Intl.ListFormat`. Add an invalid test case: `

{new Intl.ListFormat("cs").format(["Matematika"])}

`.

findings.title: Container-smoke evidence is not tied to the image or config it tested, so a PASS can outlive an nginx.conf change
findings.evidence: `docs/qa/container-smoke-latest.md` records only start/finish times, the check count and the result. It has no commit SHA, image digest or nginx.conf/Dockerfile hash, and nothing in `qa:verify` or the gate scripts checks that it is fresh (only package.json refers to the smoke). If someone later adds an `add_header` inside `location /api/` (which drops the http-level CSP and nosniff on API responses) or loosens `server_name`, the committed evidence file still says PASS for 'the refusal carries the security headers'. tasks.md 4.4 cites this file as the evidence for those claims. The static test in container-config.test.ts guards most of this, but the evidence the live behaviour claim points to can go stale silently, which the done-claims-need-evidence rule forbids.
findings.suggestion: Write `git rev-parse HEAD`, a dirty flag and a sha256 of nginx.conf and Dockerfile (or the built image ID) into the evidence header. Have the qa battery or gate-status mark the file STALE/NOT-EARNED when those hashes don't match the working tree.

findings.title: Lint rule skips the literal arguments of every Intl.*(...).format() call, including text-bearing ones like Intl.ListFormat
findings.evidence:
Spec delta, Requirement 'Externalized UI strings': "A lint rule SHALL refuse literal UI text that it can see in `src/` (JSX, props, nested collections, call arguments, …)". Round-4 change: `if (isLocaleFormatting(node.callee)) return literalTexts(node.callee.object);`. isLocaleFormatting (line ~53) returns true for any member call whose object is `new Intl.(…)`, so the call's arguments are never checked. For `new Intl.NumberFormat(…).format(n)` that is correct. For `

{new Intl.ListFormat('cs').format(['Matematika', 'Čeština'])}

` it is not: the callee object is a NewExpression, `literalTexts` falls to `default: return []`, and the two visible Czech literals go unreported. The rule can see them in the file, so this is inside its stated reach, not one of the accepted 'variable / other module' limits. The new tests only cover numeric/date formatters (lint-rule.test.ts valid cases). Coverage (whole slice, 18 scenarios): 17 implemented, 1 partial ('API through the frontend origin': real backend problem+json, a documented follow-up), 0 missing, 0 contradicted.
findings.suggestion:
Exempt only the constructor/locale arguments: for `new Intl.X(...)` skip the NewExpression's arguments (locales and options), but still run literalTexts over the `.format(...)` / `.formatToParts(...)` call arguments (or at least for ListFormat / DisplayNames / RelativeTimeFormat). For `toLocale*`, skip only the arguments, not the receiver (as now). Add an invalid case `

{new Intl.ListFormat('cs').format(['Matematika'])}

`.

findings.title: Widened static theme guard still misses common ways to force a theme (className +=, html.dark / body token overrides)
findings.evidence: Spec: "No app source outside the vendored design system SHALL set `data-theme` or a colour scheme" and No-toggle scenario: "a route with no control reports the check as skipped … and the static source check covers it". The guard's own docstring says it covers 'a theme class set through classList or className' and 'a design token rewritten at runtime / a :root/html rule redefining a token'. By reading the regex alternatives: `document.documentElement.className += ' dark'` fails `className\s*=\s*[{"'`]` because of the '+'. `html.dark { --paper: #000 }` fails `(:root|html)\s*\{` because `.dark` sits between html and the brace. `body { --paper: #000 }` and `.dark { --paper: … }` match nothing. `classList.add(mode)` with a variable also passes. So a no-control screen (where the e2e skips) could force a theme by `className +=` plus a `html.dark` token block in app.css, and the static guard would still pass. The self-test lists only patterns the regex already matches.
findings.suggestion: Allow compound assignment (`className\s*\+?=`). Flag any selector block outside the design system that redefines a design-system colour token (e.g. `--(paper|ink|hero|…)\s*:` in any CSS rule, not just :root/html). Add these strings to the 'recognises the ways a theme can be forced' self-test.

findings.title: Container smoke checks only that the 421 refusal has the security headers, not their values; server-version check covers only the shell
findings.evidence: Spec 'Served behind one origin': "Every response SHALL carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and a Content-Security-Policy with `script-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`, and no server version." The smoke's refusal check is `['x-content-type-options','referrer-policy','content-security-policy'].every((h) => foreign.headers.get(h))`, which only tests presence. The `server` header is asserted only on `/` (`shell.headers.get('server') === 'nginx'`), not on the 421 or the proxied /api/ answer. The /api/ check also only shows the value is non-empty and not the stub's. No live check confirms nosniff / no-referrer / the CSP directives on any response. Today the static test pins the http-level directives, so this is a gap in evidence, not a broken behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Add one helper that asserts the exact values (nosniff, no-referrer, CSP containing the three directives, server === 'nginx') and run it on the shell, /assets/ 404, /api 404, the proxied /api/ answer and the 421 refusal.

result.reasoning:
I traced both cases through the code in `eslint-rules/no-literal-ui-text.js`, and the finding holds.

**Case 1: literal text inside `Intl.ListFormat` is never reported.** Take `{new Intl.ListFormat('cs').format(['Matematika','Čeština'])}`:
- `JSXExpressionContainer` calls `literalTexts(CallExpression)`.
- The callee is a MemberExpression whose object is `new Intl.ListFormat(...)`. Its callee is `Intl.ListFormat`, with `Intl` as the object, so `isLocaleFormatting` returns true (lines 56-57).
- Line 89 then returns `literalTexts(callee.object)`. That object is a NewExpression, and `literalTexts` has no case for it, so it falls to `default: []` (line 107).
- The array argument `['Matematika','Čeština']` is never visited, so this NFR-9 violation is not reported.
- Nothing else catches it. `JSXExpressionContainer` is the only path for child expressions, and `JSXText` and `JSXAttribute` do not apply here.

**Case 2: a locale string is reported as UI text.** Take `Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ').format(d)`, written without `new`:
- `callee.object` is a CallExpression, not a NewExpression, and the property `format` does not match `toLocale*` or `localeCompare`. So `isLocaleFormatting` is false.
- The rule goes to the generic branch (line 92). Calling `literalTexts` on the receiver, `Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ')`, reaches the generic CallExpression branch again.
- That branch scans the arguments, and `'cs-CZ'` contains letters, so the rule reports it as UI text.

**Why it isn't refuted:** Nothing else in the rule guards either path. The header comment (lines 20-22) says the pseudo-catalog render test is the backstop only for text reached through a variable, another module, or spread attributes. It does not list this case as a known blind spot. The mechanism is exactly as described.

**Severity:** Minor is right. This is a gap in a lint rule, the `i18n-coverage` render test partly backs it up, and `Intl.ListFormat` with literal words is an uncommon pattern.

Its callee is a MemberExpression whose object is a NewExpression with callee `Intl.ListFormat`, so isLocaleFormatting returns true (lines 56-57). Line 89 then returns literalTexts(callee.object). A NewExpression has no case in the switch, so it falls to `default: []`. The argument `['Matematika']` is never looked at, and nothing is reported. That contradicts what the rule's own header says it catches ("call receivers and arguments"), and the text really is visible UI text (NFR-9). 2) False positive. Take `Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ').format(d)`. Here callee.object is a CallExpression, not a NewExpression, so isLocaleFormatting returns false. The generic branch (lines 92-93) then recurses into the receiver `Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ')`. Its callee is `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, a MemberExpression whose object is the Identifier `Intl`, not a NewExpression, and whose property is not toLocale*. So the check fails again and the argument 'cs-CZ' is scanned. 'cs-CZ' contains letters, so it is reported as literal UI text. Nothing else catches the false negative. The rule notes that src/app/i18n-coverage.test.tsx (the pseudo-catalog render test) is the backstop, but only for text the linter cannot see, and its coverage depends on rendering. The lint gap itself is real. Impact is low. Formatting literal arrays with Intl.ListFormat is uncommon, and the false positive only makes lint noisier; it doesn't hide anything. Minor severity is right, so no change to severity.

I confirmed the mechanism in e2e/theme.spec.ts:39-50. For a native select, `choices` lists every enabled option value. Nothing else re-activates them: the outer loop moves on to control i+1. A select whose first option navigates away and whose later option sets data-theme would therefore pass. That falls short of spec.md:25, which says every select on a route is activated. Earlier review rounds (review-findings.json:45, :135) also show the select handling was added on purpose to catch a theme picker built as a select.

Two caveats limit the impact. First, one of the finding's examples is wrong: a reload that only changes the query keeps the same pathname, so it does not hit the `break`. Only a real route change does. Second, there is currently no `<select>` or combobox under src/, so the gap is latent. It weakens the test's guarantee but does not hide a bug that exists today. The core claim still holds, so minor severity is right.

The code does what the finding says. At e2e/theme.spec.ts:47-49, if any option changes the pathname, the test calls `page.goto(screen.path)` and then `break`s out of `for (const choice of choices)`, so the select's remaining options are never selected. After the navigation-back the outer loop moves on to `controls.nth(i+1)`, so later options of that select are silently skipped. A later option that set `data-theme` would go undetected. This is a real gap against the "activate every control/option" spec scenario.

It cannot happen today, though. Searching `src/` finds no `<select`, `role="combobox"` or `HTMLSelectElement`, so no screen has a select and the `choices` array is always `[null]`. One of the finding's examples is also wrong: a reload that only changes the query string keeps the same pathname, so the check at line 47 is false and the loop does not break.

This is a latent weakness in a regression guard, not a bug a user would hit, and it only matters once someone adds a select whose earlier option navigates to a new path. The mechanism is confirmed, so it is not refuted, but the severity should drop to nit.

I confirmed the gap by reading the code, but nothing in the app triggers it today.

**What the guard checks.** In `src/app/theme-source.test.ts:15-29`, the only token-redefinition patterns are `setProperty('--…')` and `(:root|html)\s*\{[^}]*--[\w-]+\s*:`. None of these inputs match any part of the regex:
